road.title: Ordering
road.description: A stooped and careful soul wearing a waistcoat the colour of old tea, leaning on a staff with notches cut for every complaint. Ignatius is a Waiter of the Old School and has not written an order down since the war, any war, and has never been right.

Ignatius is hovering near your empty plate, hoping for a review. Tell Ignatius that it was good, using Italian.

character.name: Ignatius Sprocket
character.description: A stooped and careful soul wearing a waistcoat the colour of old tea, leaning on a staff with notches cut for every complaint. Ignatius is a Waiter of the Old School and has not written an order down since the war, any war, and has never been right.

npc.narrative: At mezzogiorno you cross the piazza under a cielo grigio and reach the tavolo where Ignatius Sprocket waits, holding the vassoio like a verdict. He apologises to it in advance, for nothing yet. Behind his orecchio sits una matita, unused since the war.
npc.native: Buongiorno! Per me, un caffè, sempre. E lei, cosa desidera?
npc.translation: Good morning! For me, a coffee, always. And you, what do you want?

verdict.overallFeedback: Lovely start! You greeted Ignatius and politely said you would like to order, all in correct Italian.

objectiveResults.feedback: Well done: you politely said you would like to order with "Vorrei ordinare".
This one hasn't come up yet: you'll need to ask Ignatius what there is to eat, and he'll give you another chance later.
Not needed yet: later you'll tell Ignatius that the food was good, and you'll get another chance then.

openObjectives.prompt: Ask Ignatius what there is to eat, using Italian.
Ignatius is hovering near your empty plate, hoping for a review. Tell Ignatius that it was good, using Italian.

npc.narrative: Ignatius sets down his caffè and pats the piccolo quaderno he never writes in. Outside, the cielo is grigio, and the tavolo wobbles, so he says scusi to it. On the lavagna behind him, the menu is una lunga macchia.
npc.native: Bene, ordinare è importante. Non so cosa c'è oggi, il menù è perso. Lei ha fame?
npc.translation: Good, ordering is important. I do not know what there is today, the menu is lost. Are you hungry?

player: Si, ho fame. Cosa c'e da mangiare?

correction.text: Sì, ho fame. Cosa c'è da mangiare?
correction.translation: Yes, I'm hungry. What is there to eat?

verdict.overallFeedback: Lovely! You said you were hungry and asked what there is to eat, all in Italian. Just watch the accents on "sì" and "c'è".

objectiveResults.feedback: You asked Ignatius what there is to eat, well done; just remember the accent: c'è.
Not yet: here you tell Ignatius, in Italian, that the food was good. This will come up again later.

correction.text: Sì, ho fame. Cosa c'è da mangiare?
correction.translation: Yes, I'm hungry. What is there to eat?

openObjectives.prompt: Ignatius is hovering near your empty plate, hoping for a review. Tell Ignatius that it was good, using Italian.

npc.narrative: Un fulmine lights the finestra, and Ignatius apologises to his vassoio for the noise. La pioggia hits the tetto like a creditor. He writes nothing down, but he nods at the cucina, where the answer is kept, more or less.
npc.native: Bene, c'è formaggio e pane. Il formaggio è buono, il pane è ottimo. Lei vuole il formaggio?
npc.translation: Good, there is cheese and bread. The cheese is good, the bread is excellent. Do you want the cheese?

player: Si, il formaggio per favore. Mmm... era buono! Grazie.

correction.text: Sì, il formaggio, per favore. Mmm... era buono! Grazie.
correction.translation: Yes, the cheese, please. Mmm... it was good! Thank you.

verdict.overallFeedback: Lovely! You ordered the cheese politely and told Ignatius it was good, all in Italian. Just remember the accent on \"Sì\" (yes).

objectiveResults.feedback: Passed: "era buono" tells Ignatius the food was good, in Italian.

correction.text: Sì, il formaggio, per favore. Mmm... era buono! Grazie.
correction.translation: Yes, the cheese, please. Mmm... it was good! Thank you.

npc.narrative: Ignatius does not write the ordine down. He apologises to his matita instead, out of habit. Outside, la pioggia hammers the finestra and a lampo turns the formaggio briefly blue, while sul tavolo the piatto trembles and he steadies it con un sospiro.
npc.native: Bene, il formaggio era buono, sì. Fuori c'è un temporale forte. Lei vuole un caffè?
npc.translation: Good, the cheese was good, yes. Outside there is a strong storm. Do you want a coffee?

player: No grazie. Il temporale... no bene! Lei ha un ombrello?

npc.narrative: Ignatius looks at the finestra, where the pioggia knocks on the vetro like a creditor. Poi he pats the vecchio thing by the porta e apologises to it, piano, for the weather.
npc.native: Sì, ho un ombrello, ma è vecchio. Lei vuole il pane?
npc.translation: Yes, I have an umbrella, but it is old. Do you want the bread?

player: No, basta. Il conto, per favore. Arrivederci!

npc.narrative: Ignatius turns to la cassa and murmurs a scusa to it, the way one does before disappointing un vecchio amico. Outside, la pioggia hits la finestra, and a lampo looks in. He finds a matita and holds it like a small, unreliable witness.
npc.native: Va bene, basta. Il conto non c'è, io non scrivo. Lei vuole il mio ombrello?
npc.translation: All right, enough. There is no bill, I do not write. Do you want my umbrella?
